subtitle: Monthly horror picks for the mortally curious.

novels.title: Intercepts
novels.author: T.J. Payne (2021)
novels.vibe: A gonzo, ultra-violent horror-thriller about a viral pathogen loose on a remote Air Force radio-intercept station.
novels.summary: On a windswept Aleutian listening post, an airman starts hearing something impossible on the intercepted radio signals right as a mysterious illness begins tearing through the isolated crew. As paranoia and infection spread through the station, the survivors are cut off from any outside help with no way to know who's still human.
novels.warnings: Extreme gore and body horror, graphic violence, infection/illness themes, gun violence, claustrophobic isolation.

novels.title: Coma
novels.author: Robin Cook (1977)
novels.vibe: The medical thriller that basically invented the genre — a young doctor uncovers a horrifying conspiracy behind a string of unexplained surgical comas.
novels.summary: Medical student Susan Wheeler grows suspicious after a routine surgery leaves a patient in an unexplained coma, and her investigation turns up a disturbing pattern of similar cases at her hospital. As she digs deeper into the hospital's business dealings, she uncovers a conspiracy far more calculated and horrifying than a string of tragic accidents.
novels.warnings: Medical trauma, body horror, sexual harassment, institutional violence, death.

novels.title: The Hot Zone
novels.author: Richard Preston (1994)
novels.vibe: The nonfiction Ebola outbreak book so viscerally written it reads like horror fiction.
novels.summary: A true account of the emergence of Ebola and Marburg viruses in Africa, and the terrifying 1989 outbreak of a related filovirus among lab monkeys just outside Washington, D.C. Preston renders the biology and human toll of hemorrhagic fever in unflinching, stomach-churning detail.
novels.warnings: Graphic descriptions of illness, bodily fluids, and death; animal death; medical/biohazard horror.

novels.title: Frankenstein
novels.author: Mary Shelley (1818)
novels.vibe: The foundational mad-science horror novel — a scientist's triumph over death curdles into obsession, guilt, and monstrous consequence.
novels.summary: Victor Frankenstein, obsessed with conquering death, assembles and animates a creature from scavenged human remains, then abandons it in horror at what he's made. The creature's search for connection and revenge against his creator spirals into tragedy across the frozen reaches of Europe.
novels.warnings: Death, grief, murder, themes of abandonment and isolation, mob violence.

short_works.title: The Jaunt
short_works.author: Stephen King (1981)
short_works.vibe: A sci-fi horror short about teleportation, anesthesia, and what happens to a mind left conscious across the void.
short_works.summary: A father explains the family-friendly history of "the Jaunt," a teleportation technology that requires travelers to be sedated before use, to his children before their first trip. The story builds to a horrifying account of what happens to anyone who stays conscious during the jaunt — and what that means for the family's own journey.
short_works.warnings: Body horror, psychological horror, death, disturbing implied violence, medical/anesthesia themes.

short_works.title: Herbert West–Reanimator
short_works.author: H.P. Lovecraft (1922)
short_works.vibe: The pulpy, episodic mad-scientist novella that inspired Re-Animator — a medical student obsessed with reviving the dead.
short_works.summary: Herbert West, a brilliant and morally unmoored medical student, spends years perfecting a reagent that can reanimate dead tissue, with escalating and increasingly monstrous results. Told by his horrified assistant across a series of gruesome experiments, the story follows West's relentless pursuit of his research at any cost.
short_works.warnings: Graphic body horror, gore, grave robbing, violence, disturbing medical experimentation, period-typical racism.

short_works.title: Feed Them Silence
short_works.author: Lee Mandelo (2023)
short_works.vibe: A near-future sci-fi novella about a neuroscientist who implants herself with tech to experience a wild wolf's mind — and can't fully leave it behind.
short_works.summary: Dr. Sean Kell-Luddon uses experimental neural implant technology to link her mind to a wild wolf's, hoping to understand animal consciousness before the species disappears entirely. As the boundary between her human and lupine perspectives erodes, the experiment starts consuming her marriage, her ethics, and her sense of self.
short_works.warnings: Body/mind horror themes, animal death (referenced), relationship breakdown, ethical violation, addiction-like compulsion.

short_works.title: It Breathes, It Bleeds, It Breeds
short_works.author: EmpyrealInvective (SCP Foundation, 2018)
short_works.vibe: A viscerally gross SCP Foundation piece about an anomalous, aggressively invasive parasitic organism and the horror of containing something that wants inside you.
short_works.summary: Foundation researchers document containment procedures for an anomalous creature whose primary threat is a relentless, body-horror-driven urge to physically merge with and colonize other organisms. Told through clinical incident reports, the story builds dread through procedure and consequence rather than narrative.
short_works.warnings: Extreme body horror, parasitic/invasive imagery, graphic violence, medical/clinical horror.
